title: Trump is in office. Here are his big picture plans.
excerpt: A look back at the policy priorities covered in the February 2025 post.
author: Shari Explains
coverAlt: Original cover artwork for Trump is in office. Here are his big picture plans.
body:
## On January 20, 2025…

Donald Trump was officially inaugurated back into office as the 47th president of the United States. Trump managed to obtain a landslide win during the 2024 presidential election, where he gained the popular vote and the electoral college vote. During this election, the most important issues were the economy and immigration. Many voted red because they thought a second Trump term would be better for America. In his inaugural speech, Trump vowed to stop “catch and release” and to halt the entry of undocumented migrants on the southern border. Here is an overview of what Trump is trying to do in his next four years.

## Healthcare: ACA (Affordable Care Act)

Also known as Obamacare, it was first introduced on March 23, 2010, under the Obama Administration. Since then, it has given over 40 million Americans affordable healthcare in 40 states. Trump previously tried to repeal Obamacare during his first term, but during his bid for reelection, Vice President J.D. Vance proposed “deregulating the insurance market” and dividing the people with health risks into differing plans. This would most likely drive up prices for all.

## Taxes

In 2017, during his first administration, Trump issued the tax cuts that led to a flat corporate tax rate of 21%, capped the local and state tax deduction at $10,000 (SALT cap), and increased child credit. Trump is also proposing tax cuts on businesses and the richest Americans. Beforehand, the tax cut for corporations was 35% in the Biden administration; Trump plans to lower this to 18%. Trump also plans to lower the capital gains tax to 15% for the top 5% of earners.

## Russo-Ukrainian conflict

Trump had claimed that he would end the war between Russia and Ukraine within 24 hours since entering office, but the conflict is still ongoing. Members of Trump’s National Security Council have even expressed his inability to doctor up a peace treaty within 24 hours. The President has offered no real plan to stop the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine other than mentioning that the U.S. military should reduce its aid to Ukraine and talking about personal relationships with Putin and Zelensky.

## Tariffs

During the campaign trail, Trump had been pushing mercantilist ideals with the promise of imposing tariffs on imported goods. On February 1st, 2025, Trump had enacted tariffs on China, Canada, and Mexico. These tariffs will have an immense impact on the American economy, as average consumers will have to pay more due to companies having to cover the cost of tariffs, with inflation predicted to rise between 6%-9% with these tariffs in place. On February 1st Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau ordered retaliatory tariffs on $105 billion of U.S. goods.
